newsitem.title: JAPAN: Airbus sees Japan demand for 599 planes in 20 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Airbus sees Japan demand for 599 planes in 20 yrs.

text.p: Airbus Industrie expects demand for new aircraft by Japanese airlines to total 599 planes over the next 20 years, and Airbus hopes to supply 300 of those, Adam Brown, a vice president in charge of market forecasts, told reporters on Tuesday.

Brown said the company expects Japanese demand during the next two decades for 157 small aircraft seating 125 to 175 passengers, 62 wide-body aircraft seating 210 to 250 passengers, 226 wide-body aircraft seating 300 to 400 passengers and 154 wide-body aircraft seating more than 400 passengers.
He said Japanese airlines are prone to retire their aircraft at an earlier age, averaging 18 years, than their foreign counterparts. The world average is 23 years, he said.
He also said Airbus was closely monitoring airline deregulation by Japan's Ministry of Transport.

He said deregulation will initially put downward pressure on air ticket prices, which will have a negative impact on Japanese airlines' earnings, adding that the experience of U.S. airlines with deregulation was not very encouraging.
He advised new airline companies to avoid rapid expansion.
